Test whether the designs agree

Source: R/diagnostics.R
design_agreement.Rd

Refits the model with design_effects = TRUE, which adds an offset to the population effect mean for RCT and pre-post studies relative to DiD, and returns those offsets. They are the model's own estimate of how far each design disagrees with the DiD anchor — the assumption that all designs estimate one common effect, made checkable.

Usage

design_agreement(fit, probs = c(0.05, 0.95), quiet = FALSE)

Arguments

fit

A meta_did() fit carrying more than one design.

probs

Interval probabilities.

quiet

Suppress the refit message.

Value

A list with offsets (a data frame of design, estimate, lo, hi, n_studies) and the refitted object fit.

Details

Offsets near zero support pooling. An offset that excludes zero says the designs are not exchangeable, which may reflect a real difference (selection, different follow-up, a different estimand) or a fault in how that design is being handled. It will not tell you which.

One refit, so it costs what the original fit cost. Note that design_effects = TRUE re-references treatment_effect_mean to the DiD studies, so the pooled number from the refit is not the one to report — only the offsets.

Prefer this to fitting each design subset separately. Subsets of post-only studies have to pin the time trend at zero to be identified at all, which puts their effect on the control follow-up scale rather than the baseline scale — a difference of a factor \((1+\tilde\beta)\), around 9% at a typical trend, which is larger than the disagreement you would be looking for.

See also

plot_design_agreement()
